newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Communist chief doubts Yeltsin's ability to rule.
newsitem.headline: Communist chief doubts Yeltsin's ability to rule.

text.p: The leader of Russia's Communist Party on Monday joined other opposition leaders in suggesting that President Boris Yeltsin, in hospital with pneumonia, was not well enough to rule the country.
"It is time to stop torturing the president and let him get well in peace," Gennady Zyuganov told reporters at a protest in Moscow by teachers demanding the back pay they are owed the government.
"The legislators will soon be back (in parliament) and we will propose discussing the question of establishing basic government in the country."
He did not explain what he meant by this although he has regularly criticised the government and the president, saying they are unable to govern.
Asked whether Yeltsin should step down, he said: "We have said this for a long time. I think his close relatives, friends and close circle will say: 'Boris Nikolayevich, it is time to have a rest'".
Doctors said last week that Yeltsin's latest illness, two months after heart surgery, would not affect his ability to rule.
Zyuganov, who was out of Moscow when the 65-year-old president was taken to hospital with pneumonia last Wednesday, was beaten by Yeltsin in a presidential election last year.
The communists are the largest party in the lower house of palriament. They have criticised Yeltsin in recent weeks, but stopped short of demanding a vote of no-confidence in the president.
